claims.subject: Identity
claims.claim: KIPLING is identified by the MoD as BIDC/1490.

claims.subject: Purpose
claims.claim: Project KIPLING provided security for tactical data transmissions using CLANSMAN. The NAO records a project cost of £14 million among interim measures associated with BOWMAN delays.

claims.subject: Portable kit
claims.claim: NSN 5810-99-591-2923; catalogue description identifies a portable KIPLING kit.

claims.subject: Equipment references
claims.claim: CES46953 and CESP/46953 appear in the kit record.

claims.subject: Date
claims.claim: The catalogue assignment date is 7 November 1994. This is not proof of an exact introduction-to-service date.

claims.subject: Operator workflow
claims.claim: Former users recall typing messages, passing them securely over Clansman and printing received messages on narrow roll paper.

claims.subject: Day/date behaviour
claims.claim: Former users recall failures between stations when day/date updating or synchronisation was incorrect. The actual mechanism is not established.

claims.subject: Operational context
claims.claim: Contributors recall use in 1996–97, 1998–2000 and Telic 1, including demands for stores.

claims.subject: Training context
claims.claim: The Royal Signals journal records training on the KIPLING data-entry device in an April 1999 exercise account.
claims.consequence: Contemporary unit training account. Provides exercise context only.

claims.subject: Radio cable
claims.claim: A supplier describes a seven-pin KIPLING-to-radio cable, NSN 5995-99-662-6364. Pin assignments are not established.

claims.subject: Power cable
claims.claim: A supplier describes a KIPLING DED J4 DC cable, product code 5171351, with two-pin male and small three-pin female ends. Voltage is not established.

claims.subject: Carrying bag
claims.claim: A KIPLING DPM IRR carrying bag is listed under NSN 8465-99-300-6325. This number belongs to the bag, not the terminal.

claims.subject: Obsolescence
claims.claim: The March 2013 DIN digest lists notice 2013DIN04-027 declaring BIDC/1490 obsolete. This does not establish continuous operational use until 2013.

claims.subject: Physical design
claims.claim: Enclosure, keyboard, LCD and paper rendering are interpretive.

claims.subject: Message handling
claims.claim: Character set, lengths, stores, routing, identities, duplicate handling and ACK policy are product choices.

claims.subject: Radio medium
claims.claim: Logical channels, airtime, collisions, frame loss, timing and diagnostics are simulated.

claims.subject: Date and cryptography
claims.claim: Manual key epochs and Web Crypto AES-GCM with HKDF are modern substitutes.

claims.subject: State and printing
claims.claim: Power retention, roll capacity, wrapping, spool speed, archive and persistence are designed behaviours.

claims.subject: Unestablished details
claims.claim: manufacturer, precise enclosure and keyboard layout, display dimensions, exact screen text, processor, firmware, message and memory limits, baud rate, modulation, wire protocol, acknowledgement/retry rules, printer model and paper width, power consumption, battery endurance, cipher and key-management procedures, and the complete list of supported radio sets.
